page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor featuring 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 154 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates moderate CPU performance with weak memory and cryptographic capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded average results of 1822.38 and 7232.57 respectively. However, memory performance is constrained, with a PassMark memory score categorized as poor and a cached small-block read bandwidth of 283.11 GB/sec categorized as weak. Cryptographic performance is also a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10% at 653.26. Large-block memory read and write speeds are average at 49.0 GB/sec and 30.16 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated ARM architecture and low memory density, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without high memory demands. It is suitable for lightweight database operations, which scored in the average tier with 2832.53 operations in PassMark, and basic web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive tasks, heavy cryptography, or large language model inference, where prompt processing speeds for even a small 135M model fall into the poor performance tier.
